annotations.text:
Redrawn 2026-09-07 to concept rulings 15–44 (review round and pass 3). Where a board and the concept differ, the concept wins.

The scoping task is ONE chat, always on the left. Tabs are the task's: Agent · Result · Sources · Share · History. The plan lives in the Agent tab. The Result is the REPORT: linear text with a side outline and collapsible sections, written by assessment (6) and rewritten by a full run; before assessment the Result is the longlist (ruling 50, 2026-09-08; a report written from the longlist on demand is deferred). Baseline, Longlist (list · grid · shortlist views) and the option profiles are working views reached from it. Depth words: rapid / standard / deep, asked every time, no default.

The baseline is built first and the run PAUSES: question it in chat, then confirm the plan against it. Three depths of evidence work: the longlist reads titles and abstracts and carries a source-quality profile per option (never 'how sure'); the assessment reads the full text of the documents each shortlisted option relies on, capped; a full evidence search is a child task whose report IS the option profile, shown in place in the scoping task (one document, two homes; 2026-09-08). The report stays linear: assessed options appear as stacked verdict strips (6); the wide comparison table is the shortlist view after assessment (6c). The Sources tab is the Evidence search's Sources component with two additions: read-depth and set-aside statuses, and a By option subview (6b).

Row 4 holds the sense-check branch at rapid depth and the child-report boards. Page 2 keeps two superseded structural alternatives for reference.

Sample question: reducing the number of 16 to 24 year olds not in education, employment or training. Every figure, count, quotation and named source is placeholder sample data.

Rulings made visible:
· three kinds of constraint; an evidence-scope constraint never excludes an option (2, 4: 'no in-scope evidence')
· a design change mints a VARIANT, its own option with its own search; the parent's evidence is related evidence only (4, 6, 7)
· baseline adds 'what is contested'; premises sourced, assumptions labelled reasoning; Overton + OpenAlex only (3)
· before assessment an option shows a source-quality profile: documents by type and tier, countries, populations, outcomes; a mention is not support (4b)
· grid rows = primary lever types; ambition = a tag 'as described, not measured', tier-4 reasoning; gap messages name secondary types (5)
· the proposal is a provisional allocation of reading effort: one place per lever type present; reasons = distinct / widest implementation record / only option of its type / thin evidence, never a count (5b)
· no 'most promising' and no conditional recommendation before assessment; sorts are sorts (5)
· the do-nothing band is 'the situation these options would change', never a comparison; each effect carries its own comparator, population and period; no superlatives (6)
· transferability: retrieved / stated by you / planned by you; the weakest leg decides; a plan becomes 'Conditional on: …'; no factor fractions (6, 7)
· documents counted, not studies, until full text is read; no study-design labels (6, 6c)
· the report stays linear text: verdict strips in the report, the comparison table as a working view (6, 6c; 2026-09-08)
· unassessed kept options listed by theme; closing section 'what needs deciding or commissioning next' = unknowns only (6)
· Sources = the Evidence search Sources component + statuses 'read in full / abstract only / not read under the cap / set aside: evidence scope' + a By option subview (6b; 2026-09-08)
· one document: the child task's report is the profile, shown in place with the scoping frame around it; the child task adds Sources, plan and History (7b, 7c; 2026-09-08)
· inherit is shared: the child Evidence search inherits the option's design, documents, light findings, user context and evidence scope from the scoping task, re-screens and searches beyond (7b, 7c, 7d; ruling 48)
· sense-check = an entry branch; rapid = the named option alone through 'Assess'; questions to put to the department (8)

Moments between the journey boards, added 2026-09-08 from the owner-approved refinement pass (ChatGPT review, ported in the ruled design language): the baseline confirmed and the longlist generating, with the next action in view (3b); a direct edit on the shortlist view with its consequence named and Undo (5c); a plan change after assessment, the prior report readable and labelled, with Refresh affected results and Undo; the refresh in progress; and the History view of what changed after a full search, before and now.

Refinements ported onto the journey boards: 'Hide chat' (the built app already collapses the chat); the plan's constraints as a table with what happens and when it is checked; the baseline's 'check the target population' callout; counts corrected (14 included; seven reviewed, five with outcome evidence, seven kept unassessed); top lines that lead with findings, a limitation and the next decision; the Sources filters grouped as Screening · Reading · Use with a Source quality column; the profile's how-sure and transferability block and key-assumption box at the top; questions for the department straight after the sense-check top line.

Not adopted, by owner ruling: the pack's restyle (desaturated blue, Arial, radii, small text), status chips, viewport-clipped boards, and renaming 'Do nothing' (kept, as 'Do nothing: current policy and trajectory').

Two structural alternatives to the leading direction, both conversation-first, kept for reference.

A · Everything inline: living cards sit in the chat; superseded versions collapse to a stub.

B · Stage rail: each stage has its own chat and artifact.

Both were superseded on 2026-09-07 by the hybrid on page 1: the report is the Result, the stages are working views reached from it, and the chat stays the spine.
